The Lesna Icon of the Theotokos

Icons

Theotokos

The Lesna Icon of the Theotokos

Lesninskaya · Lesna stone icon

What is depictedHistory and traditionPublished explanationSources

The Lesna received history begins with a shepherd finding a radiant image in a pear tree in 1683. ROCOR’s shrine account identifies it as a carved stone icon kept in France.

[1] Discovery

What is depicted

The photograph shows the named Lesna shrine image within a large oval metal setting. The small crowned Mother-and-Child relief lies at its centre. Father Maxim Massalitin is credited for this photograph; his photographic licence is distinct from the age of the historical carved object and from later ornament or restoration.

[2] Displayed work;file-level title,description,date and visual identification

History and tradition

The OCA recounts transfers between Orthodox and Catholic custody in the Lesna region, including an Orthodox women’s monastery established in 1885. Its account describes healing and other miracle traditions and gives September 8 and Pentecost as additional observances. The institutional history is that publication’s account, not a summary judgment about every disputed local memory.

[1] Custody,monastery and observances

ROCOR’s published description calls the image a carving in a dark-red oval stone. It identifies the discovery on September 14, 1683 and locates the shrine at Lesna Convent in Provemont, France. This identifies the historical object represented by the modern photograph without dating every part of its decorative mount to 1683.

[3] Section The Lesna Icon of the Mother of God

Published explanation

The OCA associates the icon’s discovery with the Exaltation of the Cross. That printed church commemoration provides its calendar context. The source’s devotional reputation and the image photographer’s reuse permission are different kinds of evidence and remain separately cited.

[1] Opening and concluding commemoration
